2609.18905.title: Structured Claim-Level Discourse Representations for Dense Health Narratives
2609.18905.paper_summary: Health discourse in social media videos often contains densely entangled claims spanning multiple thematic aspects, stances, evidential frames, and rhetorical functions within short conversational spans. Existing approaches largely rely on coarse topic-level, sentiment-based, or stance-oriented representations that do not adequately capture this structure. Our analysis identifies an average of 13.22 atomic claims per minute, motivating richer claim-level discourse representations. We introduce a structured framework for claim-level discourse analysis in dense health narratives. Our framework models discourse through tuples linking atomic claims with thematic aspects, stance, and multidimensional pragmatic discourse attributes. To support this setting, we construct a benchmark spanning four health domains with 1,191 manually annotated claims from 60 videos. Using this framework, we evaluate automated structured discourse analysis under different discourse context settings. Results show that current LLMs achieve strong performance on thematic categorization and stance prediction, but struggle with high-dimensional pragmatic profiling. We also find that different discourse tasks benefit from different forms of contextual reasoning, suggesting that future systems may require task decomposition and specialized inference strategies.
2609.18905.paper_summary_zh: 社交媒體視頻中的健康話語通常包含密集交織的主張，涵蓋多個主題方面、立場、證據框架和修辭功能，並在短暫的對話中展開。現有的方法主要依賴粗略的主題級別、基於情感或面向立場的表徵，這些方法無法充分捕捉這種結構。我們的分析識別出每分鐘平均有 13.22 條原子主張，這促使我們對主張級別的話語表徵進行更豐富的探索。我們引入了一個結構化框架，用於在密集的健康敘事中進行主張級別的話語分析。我們的框架通過將原子主張與主題方面、立場和多維語用話語屬性連結的元組來建模話語。為了支持這一設置，我們構建了一個基準，涵蓋四個健康領域，包含來自 60 個視頻的 1,191 條手動標註的主張。利用這一框架，我們在不同的話語上下文設置下評估自動化的結構化話語分析。結果顯示，當前的 LLM 在主題分類和立場預測上表現出色，但在高維語用特徵分析上則面臨挑戰。我們還發現，不同的話語任務受益於不同形式的上下文推理，這表明未來的系統可能需要任務分解和專門的推理策略。
